primitives.name: GrieferLens
primitives.verbatim_quote: Index Terms: MOBA Games—Griefers; Visualization—Visual Analytics; 1 INTRODUCTION Multiplayer Online Battle Arenas (MOBAs) are a popular genre of esports, with games like League of Legends (LoL) hosting professional tournaments on an international scale and generating over two billion US dollars in annual game revenue [1].
primitives.assumptions: Assumes manual review as baseline, lacks standardized criteria, and relies on video-based labeling.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down complex spatiotemporal MOBA data into structured behavioral metrics.

layer2.mapping: Maps visual analytics pipeline to GSI conformal prediction intervals for griefer probability.
layer2.telemetry: Match-level behavioral feature vectors fed into anomaly detection models.

primitives.name: Player Summary View
primitives.verbatim_quote: It consists of Player Summary View and Match Replay View.
primitives.assumptions: Operates under the premise that player trajectories can be quantified and compared.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Aggregates individual player actions into composite scores.

layer2.mapping: Derives state-transition matrices from replay data for GSE.
layer2.telemetry: Normalized action frequencies per minute, used as input features.

primitives.name: Match Replay View
primitives.verbatim_quote: (b) Match Replay View summarizes the whole match progress and enables users to check the detailed events of one player and contextualize its trajectory with other players.
primitives.assumptions: Presumes replay data is complete and accurate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Replays enable temporal correlation analysis between griefing events.

layer2.mapping: Translates replay data into state-action-reward sequences for Markov decision processes.
layer2.telemetry: Event timestamp synchronization across all players.

primitives.name: Spatiotemporal Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given the complexity of the multi-variant spatiotemporal data for MOBA games, game developers heavily rely on manual review of entire game video recordings to label and annotate griefers, which is a time-consuming process.
primitives.assumptions: Treats game maps as homogeneous Euclidean spaces with discrete time steps.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Analyzes movement patterns and event timing across game phases.

layer2.mapping: Applies sequential pattern mining to identify non-participation signatures.
layer2.telemetry: Average distance traveled per minute, used as proxy for engagement.

primitives.name: Griefer Detection Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: 2 SYSTEM OVERVIEW GrieferLens focuses on identifying six types of griefers, as proposed and summarized by experts: AFK, feeding, lane stealing, jungle stealing, non-participation, and position stealing.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G': 'set of griefer types {AFK, feeding, lane_stealing, jungle_stealing, non_participation, position_stealing}', 'P': 'set of players in match', 'T': 'temporal duration of match'}
primitives.assumptions: Players exhibit deterministic behavioral patterns; griefer types are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When observed behavior deviates beyond rule-based thresholds with confidence >90%.

layer2.mapping: Maps player activity logs to griefer type probabilities via expert-defined heuristics and temporal event clustering.
layer2.telemetry: Probability vector over G for each P ∈ P

primitives.name: Behavior Trajectory Synthesis
primitives.verbatim_quote: The trajectories of each player are also provided to help users understand the dynamics of match progress.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X(t)': 'spatial coordinates of player at time t', 'V(t)': 'velocity vector of player at time t', 'M': 'match duration'}
primitives.assumptions: Player movement is continuous and differentiable over time intervals.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At singularities where X(t) exhibits abrupt changes without external stimulus.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphs player motion to phase space for anomaly detection using dynamical systems theory.
layer2.telemetry: Phase-space density maps per player over T

primitives.name: Rule-Filtered Alerts
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given the indeterministic nature of griefer behavior's definition, experts agreed that the first step in identifying griefers should be to use our algorithm's filtered output, which has been proven to reach a reasonable false-negative rate (≤10%).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F': 'filtered alert function', 'FN': 'false negative rate ≤ 0.1', 'A': 'alert vector for player set'}
primitives.assumptions: Alert generation is governed by fixed rules derived from expert consensus.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When FN exceeds threshold due to ambiguous or novel griefer behaviors.

layer2.mapping: Filters raw behavioral data through expert-defined heuristics to generate preliminary griefer indicators.
layer2.telemetry: Binary alert flags A_i ∈ {0,1} for each player i

primitives.name: Multi-Perspective Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: The system integrates domain experts' knowledge to provide an overview analysis of players' behavior and synthesizes the key events during a match from both temporal and spatial perspectives.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'spatial perspective matrix', 'T': 'temporal event log', 'E': 'event synthesis operator'}
primitives.assumptions: Synthesis of S and T under E preserves causal coherence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When temporal and spatial views are inconsistent or contradictory.

layer2.mapping: Maps combined spatial-temporal data to a unified behavioral profile using event graph theory.
layer2.telemetry: Behavioral profile vector B_i for each player i

It builds upon prior work that emphasized maintaining game balance through understanding Snowballing and Comeback events, yet acknowledges a gap in systematic detection of deliberate disruption. The core innovation lies in combining domain expert knowledge with automated filtering to reduce reliance on manual video annotation. The system operates by generating rule-based alerts, analyzing player trajectories, and synthesizing multi-perspective behavioral summaries. The integration of temporal and spatial data allows for nuanced interpretation of player behavior, supporting a more robust and scalable solution than traditional methods.
